TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Sub-committee FROM: Marc B. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: February 3, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of FY26 Tuition and Mandatory Fees Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action is to approve FY26 tuition and mandatory fees. As a reminder, the Board of Trustees approved the shifting of final approval of tuition and fees to February 2024 (and in February thereafter) in their September 2023 meeting. Recommendation and Points to Consider: URI is proposing a 3.5% increase in tuition across all student types, and a 0.7% increase in undergraduate mandatory fees. Based on model assumptions, this level of increase optimizes resource to offset critical university operations while keeping URI education accessible and limiting potential enrollment declines. Supporting Information: See enclosure. Proposed Motion of the Board: To recommend approval of a tuition increase of 3.5% for in-state students and 3.5% for out-of-state students and increase fee rates, as presented in the enclosure, representing a 0.7% increase in total fees.

Total Cost of Attendance (TCOA) 3 The Board is responsible for evaluating rates as they relate to a student’s total cost of attendance (TCOA) and approving mandatory tuition and fees. TCOA is defined as: • Tuition • Mandatory fees • “Standard” housing and dining charges (most likely to be selected) for a given student. • Standard housing refers to Group B Double • Standard dining refers to the Unlimited Standard Plan • Students are also charged a housing-specific communications fee

10 Tuition Recommendations and Assumptions

Recommendation and Items for Consideration Recommendation: • Approve 3.5% tuition increase for in-state and 3.5% tuition increase for out-of-state students • Based on model assumptions, this level of increase optimizes resources to offset critical operations while keeping URI education accessible and limiting potential enrollment declines • Must be considered within the context of URI’s ability to effectively reach Strategic Plan KPIs • Unprecedented market conditions (post-COVID, FAFSA impacts, in-state tuition programs offered within neighboring states, inflationary environment) increases risk of volatility in assumptions

Assumptions • Enrollment decline assumptions: • Once tuition reaches a 4% increase year-over-year, enrollment decreases anywhere from 1-2% • Items to consider: • Enrollment decline assumptions applied to all student types, but based on different factors for in-state and out-of-state students • Tuition and fee percentage increases are the same across all student types, but the dollar amount impacts differ based on base tuition and fees • Every 0.5% of enrollment loss equates to loss of ($1.1m) in tuition, net of financial aid
